content.body:
Tagline: Verify AI-written code with execution evidence, not another LLM opinion.

First comment (owner posts immediately after launch): "I built CodeVetter because every AI reviewer I tried graded my agent's diff with another model reading the same diff. CodeVetter actually exercises the change — builds, tests, browser/API behavior — through a deterministic Rust engine and gives you a replayable evidence bundle. Runs entirely on your Mac: desktop app, CLI, and a read-only MCP server so Claude Code/Codex can verify their own work. No code leaves your machine. It's open source — would love feedback on the verification approach.",

Topics: Developer Tools, Artificial Intelligence, Open Source.

Required before launch: PH maker profile, 3-5 gallery images (app screenshots from apps/macos + a terminal evidence-bundle shot), a 60-90s demo video or GIF loop.

content.body:
Title: Show HN: CodeVetter – verify AI-written code with execution evidence, not an LLM's opinion

Text (optional body, keep short): I kept watching AI code reviewers grade my agent's work by having another model read the same diff. CodeVetter takes a different approach: it exercises the change — build, tests, browser/API behavior — via a deterministic Rust engine, then emits an inspectable evidence bundle you can replay. Local-first macOS app + CLI + read-only MCP server (so your coding agent can verify its own work). Open source.

Post timing: Tue–Thu, ~8-9am PT. Owner posts from own account. Do not ask for upvotes anywhere — instant kill. Reply to every comment in the first 4 hours.

content.body:
Title: I built a Mac app that verifies AI-written code by actually running it — not by asking another LLM

Body: Every AI code reviewer I tried grades the diff with another model reading the same diff. CodeVetter exercises the change instead: builds, tests, browser/API behavior through a deterministic Rust engine, then emits a replayable evidence bundle. Local-first (nothing leaves your machine), open source, and there's a read-only MCP server so Claude Code/Codex can verify their own output. Feedback welcome — especially on what evidence you'd actually trust.
